steps.description:
Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

Create a program that asks the user to enter 2 integers in a row. If both integers are greater than 10, display "both greater than 10". Otherwise, display "not both are greater than 10".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

11 10

10 11

10 10

11 11

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 integers: 11 10 not both are greater than 10

Example 2 Input 2 integers: 10 11 not both are greater than 10

Example 3 Input 2 integers: 10 10 not both are greater than 10

Example 4 Input 2 integers: 11 11 both are greater than 10

Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

Create a program that asks the user to enter 2 integers in a row. If both integers are greater than 10, display both numbers. If only one integer is greater than 10, display that integer. Otherwise, display "none".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

11 10

10 11

77 10

10 99

15 21

10 10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 integers: 11 10 11

Example 2 Input 2 integers: 10 11 11

Example 3 Input 2 integers: 77 10 77

Example 4 Input 2 integers: 10 99 99

Example 5 Input 2 integers: 15 21 15 21

Example 6 Input 2 integers: 10 10 none

Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

Create a program that asks the user to enter an integer. If it is within 5 to 10, display "in range", else display "out of range".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

4

11

5

10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter an integer: 4 out of range

Example 2 Enter an integer: 11 out of range

Example 3 Enter an integer: 5 in range

Example 4 Enter an integer: 10 in range

none

Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

Create a program that asks the user to enter an integer. If it is less than or equal to 5, or it is more than 10, display "in range". Otherwise, display "out of range".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

4

5

6

10

11

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter an integer: 4 in range

Example 2 Enter an integer: 5 in range

Example 3 Enter an integer: 6 out of range

Example 4 Enter an integer: 10 out of range

Example 5 Enter an integer: 11 in range

Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

Create a program that asks the user to enter a float number. If it is between 0.5 to 1.5 (i.e. excluding 0.5 and 1.5), display "in range A". If it is from 1.5 to 2.5 (i.e. including 1.5 and 2.5), display "in range B". Otherwise, display "out of range"

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

0.5

1.4

1.5

2.51

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter a float: 0.5 out of range

Example 2 Enter a float: 1.4 in range A

Example 3 Enter a float: 1.5 in range B

Example 4 Enter a float: 2.51 out of range

Make use of the and/or operators in this question.

The scale below determines if a person is having fever based on his/her body temperature in degree celsius: hypothermia below 35 normal 35 to 37 slight fever above 37 to 38 high fever above 38

Create a program that asks the user to enter his or her body temperature in degrees celsius. Referring to the scale above, display "hypothermia", "normal", "slight fever" or "high fever" based on his body temperature.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

34.9

35

37

37.1

38

38.10

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input temperature (degree celsius): 34.9 hypothermia

Example 2 Input temperature (degree celsius): 35 normal

Example 3 Input temperature (degree celsius): 37 normal

Example 4 Input temperature (degree celsius): 37.1 slight fever

Example 5 Input temperature (degree celsius): 38 slight fever

Example 6 Input temperature (degree celsius): 38.1 high fever
